plz.title: Postcode & premium region
plz.oneLiner: Sets your premium region — premiums differ by municipality, not just by canton.
plz.short: Your premium depends on where you live. Many cantons are split into two or three premium regions, and the region that applies is determined by the municipality, not the postcode alone. If a postcode covers several municipalities, you pick yours.

birthYear.title: Birth year & age group
birthYear.short: Premiums differ across three age groups: children (0–18), young adults (19–25), and adults (26+). Your birth year sets your age group, and with it the deductible tiers available to you.

franchise.title: Deductible (Franchise)
franchise.oneLiner: A higher deductible lowers your monthly premium.
franchise.short: The deductible is the share of your medical costs you pay yourself each year before the insurer starts paying. Adults choose between CHF 300 and CHF 2500. A high deductible means a lower premium but more out-of-pocket risk if you need care. The coverage is identical either way.

unfalldeckung.title: Accident coverage
unfalldeckung.short: Basic insurance normally also covers accidents. If you're employed at least 8 hours a week by an employer, you're covered for accidents through them and can exclude accident coverage from your health insurer — which lowers the premium slightly. If unsure, leave it included.

models.title: Insurance models
models.short: You choose between the standard model (free choice of doctor) and a cheaper alternative model with a set first point of contact. The coverage is the same everywhere.

guide.lead: Basic insurance (OKP) is mandatory and, by law, identical at every insurer. So you're only comparing price, model, and service — not the scope of coverage.

rules.heading: The rules everyone follows
rules.item1: Basic insurance is mandatory. After you move to Switzerland you have three months to take out cover — it applies retroactively to your arrival date.
rules.item2: Every insurer must accept you for basic insurance. There are no health questions and no rejections.
rules.item3: You can switch insurer once a year. Your cancellation must reach your current insurer by 30 November; the switch takes effect on 1 January.
rules.item4: The scope of coverage is set by law and is the same everywhere. A cheaper insurer is not less insurance.

praemienGuide.h1: Swiss health insurance premiums {year}: what you need to know
praemienGuide.intro: The Federal Office of Public Health (FOPH) publishes the new premiums at the end of September each year. How much they rise or fall depends on the previous year's healthcare costs, the canton and the insurer you choose — there is no single Swiss premium.
praemienGuide.projected: For {projYear}, Comparis expects an average premium increase of {comparis}%, and the FOPH {bagLow}–{bagHigh}% (as of {asOf}).

howSet.heading: How the premium is made up
howSet.intro: Every insurer calculates its premiums using the same factors set by law:
howSet.region: Canton of residence and premium region — depending on healthcare costs in the region.
howSet.age: Age group — children (0–18), young adults (19–25) and adults (26+) pay different premiums.
howSet.franchise: Deductible — a higher deductible (up to CHF 2500) lowers the monthly premium, but you cover more of the costs yourself.
howSet.model: Insurance model — standard, family doctor, Telmed or HMO; a restricted choice of providers lowers the premium.
howSet.accident: Accident coverage — if you are already covered against accidents through your employer, you can exclude it from your health insurance.

deadlines.heading: Key deadlines
deadlines.text: You can switch insurers once a year. Your cancellation must reach your current insurer by 30 November; the switch takes effect on 1 January.

faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: When do I have to switch insurers?
faq.a1: Your cancellation must reach your current insurer by 30 November at the latest. The switch to the new insurer then takes effect on 1 January of the following year.
faq.q2: Do premiums go up every year?
faq.a2: Not necessarily, but usually. Premiums follow actual healthcare costs — in most years they rise, but the amount varies widely by canton and insurer.
faq.a3: The deductible is the annual amount you pay yourself for treatment costs before your insurer starts to pay. It ranges from CHF 300 to CHF 2500 — a higher deductible lowers the monthly premium.
faq.q4: What does the standard model mean?
faq.a4: In the standard model you can freely choose any licensed doctor. Alternative models (family doctor, Telmed, HMO) restrict that choice and are cheaper in return.
faq.q5: Can an insurer turn down my application?
faq.a5: No. In basic insurance every insurer must accept you — there are no health questions and no rejection.
